title: Inner closed-support restriction for one full root-tower term
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a characteristic-$p$ field $k$, a finite norm-topological extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. For $F=E,\Omega$ use the condensed ring $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ of all continuous maps, its pullbacks $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$, and internal modules and ordinary unbounded derived direct images [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Sites are small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $B\to Y$ an affine etale chart with boundary the reduced strict normal crossings divisor $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$, whose branches are exactly $V(t_d)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$ be affine pro-etale, put $S=U\times_B V(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$, and set
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_{d,n}]_{1\le d\le r}/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_d\right).$$
The index consists of positive integers prime to $p$, ordered by divisibility, and the transition for $n\mid m$ sends $x_{d,n}$ to $x_{d,m}^{m/n}$. Let $i:S\to T$ set every root to zero. Partition $\{1,\ldots,r\}=I_o\sqcup I_i$ with $I_i\ne\varnothing$. Let $V\subset U$ invert all outer parameters and let $W\subset V$ invert all parameters. Put $T^\circ=T\times_UW$. Write $a:V\hookrightarrow U$ and let $h:Z\hookrightarrow V$ be the reduced closed complement of $W$ in $V$.
Let $\mathcal N$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{F,T}$-module and specify $i^*\mathcal N\cong p_S^*M_F$, where $M$ is a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space and $M_F(Q)=C(Q,F\otimes_E M)$ uses the finite-dimensional product norm topology [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. For a profinite set $P$ use $X[P]=\varprojlim_{P\twoheadrightarrow P_d}\coprod_{P_d}X$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. Let $f_P:T^\circ[P]\to V$ be the structural map, let $\mathcal N_P$ be the pullback of $\mathcal N$ to $T^\circ[P]$, and put $K_P=R(f_P)_*(\mathcal N_P[0])$. Use the actual closed adjunction unit $\eta_h:K_P\to h_*h^*K_P$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Write $s:S\hookrightarrow U$.
Let $C_F[P]$ denote the free internal $C_F$-module on $Q\mapsto C(Q,P)$; internal Hom is right adjoint to internal module tensor, and its right derived functor is derived in its second variable. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\sigma_P:s^*Ra_*h_*h^*K_P\ \cong\ p_S^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_F).$$
If $\alpha_P:s^*R(af_P)_*(\mathcal N_P[0])\cong p_S^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_F)$ is the restriction-of-sections comparison of [lem-sfb-root-tower-boundary-acyclicity], then, inserting the canonical derived composition identification, one has
$$\sigma_P\circ s^*Ra_*(\eta_{h,K_P})=\alpha_P.$$
The isomorphisms and equality are natural in $P$, in maps of the supplied lisse extensions, and under pro-etale base change of $U$. They commute with continuous profinite families of automorphisms of the root tower and equivariant actions on $\mathcal N$: compatibility for a family parametrized by a profinite $Q$ is equality on the $Q$-parametrized terms, not only on its points. The assertion includes $I_o=\varnothing$ and rank zero. No descent along the root-cover nerve and no group invariants are asserted.

proof.text: Let $q_P:T[P]\to U$ be the unpunctured structural map and $H_P=Rq_{P,*}\mathcal N_P[0]$. On $T[P]$ invert the outer parameters, obtaining $l:T_V[P]\hookrightarrow T[P]$ and $q_{V,P}:T_V[P]\to V$; then invert the inner ones, obtaining $j:T^\circ[P]\hookrightarrow T_V[P]$. The puncture-invariance input applied on $T_V[P]$ with subset $I_i$ identifies $\mathcal N_P|_{T_V[P]}[0]$ with $Rj_*\mathcal N_P|_{T^\circ[P]}[0]$. Its hypotheses hold after localizing $B$ at the outer parameters: the remaining boundary is the inner one, and the already adjoined outer roots are an affine pro-etale extension there. Hence $K_P\cong Rq_{V,P,*}\mathcal N_P|_{T_V[P]}[0]$. Applying puncture invariance on $T[P]$ with $I_o$ and then derived composition identifies $Ra_*K_P\cong H_P$. All these identifications use inverses of the actual open units; composition uses the conjugate of the exact inverse-image composition. Thus they keep the adjunction normalization and not just the objects.

proof.text:
For each nonempty $J\subseteq I_i$ put $U_J=V_U(t_j:j\in J)$, $V_J=U_J\cap V$, with inclusions $g_J:U_J\hookrightarrow U$ and $d_J:V_J\hookrightarrow V$. Define $T_J$ by setting the roots indexed by $J$ to zero, as in the coordinate-face input, and denote the restricted lisse module by $\mathcal N_{J,P}$. Apply its $\beta_{J,P}$ over $V$ to the unpunctured presentation of $K_P$ in step 1. This gives $d_J^*K_P\cong Rq_{V_J,P,*}\mathcal N_{J,P}|_{T_{V_J}[P]}[0]$. Exactness of the closed direct image and derived composition turn $Ra_*d_{J,*}d_J^*K_P$ into the structural image of this restriction on $U$. Apply puncture invariance to the tower $T_J[P]$ with subset $I_o$: its chart is the regular intersection of the branches indexed by $J$, its remaining boundary parameters are those outside $J$, and $U_J$ is its affine pro-etale pullback. This application is local on that chart: discard empty branches and choose affine open neighborhoods on which the restricted components are the branches; the resulting comparisons glue because they are the actual open units. The defining regular-intersection clause of the strict normal crossings boundary supplies precisely this regularity. We get
$$Ra_*d_{J,*}d_J^*K_P\cong g_{J,*}R(q_{J,P})_*\mathcal N_{J,P}[0]\cong g_{J,*}g_J^*H_P.$$
The last comparison is the coordinate-face input over $U$. Its adjunct-unit normalization identifies $Ra_*$ of the closed unit $K_P\to d_{J,*}d_J^*K_P$ with the closed unit $H_P\to g_{J,*}g_J^*H_P$ under step 1. Compatibility for nested faces identifies all restriction maps in these diagrams as well.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: compute each inner intersection and normalize its unit

proof.text: The closed subschemes $V_{\{d\}}$, $d\in I_i$, cover $Z$ as closed subsets: a prime contains the product of the inner parameters if and only if it contains one of them. They factor through the reduced $Z$: apply [lem-sfb-snc-root-limit-normal-charts] with no root parameters to each regular finite-type divisor chart and its weakly etale algebra $R/(t_d)$. It gives normality, hence reducedness, of this algebra. Indeed a nilpotent vanishes in every domain prime localization, and therefore vanishes in the ring. A map from this reduced divisor to the scheme-theoretic union annihilates its nilradical and so factors through $Z$. Their nonempty intersections are $V_J$. Their complementary opens are quasi-compact, being finite unions of principal opens on the affine localization $V$. Apply the finite closed-cover resolution to $K_P$ on $V$ and $h:Z\hookrightarrow V$. It applies to this derived object using a nonnegative representative, since $K_P$ is the right derived direct image of a module in degree zero. Its augmentation identifies $\eta_{h,K_P}$ with the augmentation into the finite alternating complex of the $d_{J,*}d_J^*K_P$. Apply $Ra_*$ and then $s^*$. A finite total complex is formed by finitely many shifts and cones, which these derived functors preserve. Step 2 identifies its terms with $s^*g_{J,*}g_J^*H_P$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: resolve the reduced inner union using closed intersections, preserving the original unit

proof.text:
Every $g_J$ contains $S$, so write $s=g_Js_J$. By the invertible closed counit,
$$s^*g_{J,*}g_J^*H_P\cong s_J^*g_J^*g_{J,*}g_J^*H_P\cong s_J^*g_J^*H_P=s^*H_P.$$
The triangle identity sends the restriction of the unit $H_P\to g_{J,*}g_J^*H_P$ to the identity of $s^*H_P$. Hence every term and every face map of step 3 is the constant diagram on $A_P=s^*H_P$, with its signed alternating differential, and its augmentation is the diagonal identity. In particular this is a statement about the actual map induced by $\eta_h$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: closed counit and triangle identity trivialize the restricted finite diagram

proof.text:
Choose the least element $d_0$ of the nonempty ordered set $I_i$. For an abelian group (or sheaf) $G$, the augmented alternating complex of nonempty subsets of $I_i$ with constant value $G$, identity face maps and augmentation the diagonal, is contractible. Explicitly, for an alternating cochain $c$, extended by antisymmetry and by zero on repeated indices, put $(Hc)(a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1})=c(d_0,a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1})$; in degree zero $H$ is evaluation at $d_0$ into the augmentation object. In $dH+Hd$ the terms deleting an $a_j$ cancel in pairs, and deleting $d_0$ leaves $c$; this also covers the augmented degree $-1$. Step 4 identifies the terms with $A_P$ and the face maps with identities only in the derived category, so do not contract at chain level. Filter the augmented finite total complex of step 3, after $s^*Ra_*$, by horizontal degree; this filtration has finitely many steps and each graded piece is a shifted term, so the exact triangulated functor $s^*Ra_*$ carries it to a finite tower of distinguished triangles. Its first-page differentials are induced by the horizontal maps. On each cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^q$ the first page is therefore the constant augmented alternating complex on $\mathcal H^q(A_P)$ with diagonal augmentation, which the homotopy $H$ contracts. A finitely filtered complex whose first page is exact is acyclic, so the cone of the augmentation $A_P\to s^*Ra_*(\text{total complex})$ is zero and the augmentation is an isomorphism. Steps 1--4 now show that
$$\delta_P=s^*Ra_*(\eta_{h,K_P}):s^*R(af_P)_*\mathcal N_P[0]\longrightarrow s^*Ra_*h_*h^*K_P$$
is invertible: its composite with the step-3 isomorphism onto the total complex is this augmentation. This elementary argument uses a finite complex only.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: explicit simplex contraction proves invertibility of the supported restriction map

proof.text: Let $B_P=p_S^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[P],M_F)$. The boundary-acyclicity node gives the specified restriction-of-sections isomorphism $\alpha_P:s^*R(af_P)_*\mathcal N_P[0]\cong B_P$: its chart is $B$, its affine pro-etale object is $U$, its full boundary intersection is $S$, and its lisse extension and boundary trivialization are exactly the supplied ones. Define $\sigma_P=\alpha_P\delta_P^{-1}$. This is an isomorphism and associativity gives $\sigma_P\delta_P=\alpha_P$, with the canonical derived composition from step 1. Consequently the required normalization follows from the given comparison, rather than from a new choice of target identification.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion: define the normalized supported comparison by the given boundary comparison

proof.text: Naturality of the actual closed unit makes $\delta_P$ a natural transformation. Steps 1--4 use the natural open units, coordinate-face comparisons, and the natural finite closed-cover augmentation, so their identifications commute with maps of $P$, maps of supplied extensions, and pro-etale base change of $U$. For a profinite family indexed by $Q$, apply those same constructions to the $Q$-parametrized terms; the family clauses of the two root-tower inputs identify the entire diagrams, including their units. Thus the equality for $\delta_P$ holds on these terms. The boundary comparison has exactly this family naturality as well. Inverting a natural isomorphism preserves its commuting squares, so $\sigma_P=\alpha_P\delta_P^{-1}$ has every required naturality and equivariance. The temporary choice $d_0$ proves invertibility only and occurs in neither $\delta_P$ nor $\sigma_P$. If $I_o$ is empty, the outer open unit is the identity and the argument still applies. With one inner branch the finite resolution has one term. If $S$ is empty both sides are zero on its site. Rank zero gives zero throughout. No step uses a root-nerve totalization or group invariants.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NV-04c71912c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery; it gets two small repairs. This is a first split, not a re-split: there is no repair note, and the item was unsplit with the same statement on the N6 snapshots. Its source, blueprint main-20261015 ctf-stability direct-images proof paragraph (3), gives no root-tower argument, so labelling the proof as agent-written is correct. The proof works. Step 1: puncture invariance applies with base V, which is affine pro-etale over B, first for the inner subset and then for the outer subset on T, giving Ra_*K_P ≅ H_P. Step 2: coordinate-face applies directly over V for every J inside the inner index set. Puncture invariance on T_J uses the regular face chart V(t_J), with Zariski localization when branches are disconnected or empty, and the adjunct clause matches the units. Step 3: the V_d cover Z and their complements are quasi-compact principal opens. Normal-charts with no roots gives reducedness, and the closed-cover augmentation is the closed unit. Step 4: the closed counit and triangle identity make every term and face map constant. Step 6: sigma is alpha times delta inverse, and boundary-acyclicity matches the same chart, U, S, module and trivialization. Step 7: naturality holds before inversion. The three new nodes are statement-only, true as far as I can test, not duplicates and not restatements of the item. Puncture invariance follows from Abhyankar on the regular Kummer levels plus pro-p wild inertia with l different from p. Coordinate-face is integral closed base change plus topological invariance, checked on r=1. The closed-cover resolution holds in any ringed topos: by Stacks 09AH it reduces to Mayer-Vietoris for subterminal objects. Fixes: (E5) step 5 contracted a strictly constant double complex, but step 4 identifies the terms only in the derived category. It now filters the finite total complex by columns and contracts the first page on cohomology sheaves. (B3) The closed-cover node now cites def-weil-closed-immersion in its statement and stmt_deps. Batch 5: def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary is a general SNC definition, not part of the trace-formula or Poincare-duality proofs, and the item already cited it on base, so it is accepted.
